concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: x-t, v-t, a-t graphs — reading and interpretation

level_scope.hs_physics: Core mechanics questionnaire (036-361) topic; almost every exam includes at least one kinematics item. Expect x-t/v-t graph reading, free-fall, and the four kinematic equations in multi-part word problems.
Bagrut mechanics expects independent x/y motion analysis and relative-velocity setups (e.g., boats, aircraft). Questions combine vector components with 1D kinematic equations rather than calculus.

concepts.name: Projectile Motion
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Decomposing initial velocity into x and y components
Velocity at any time (components and magnitude)

level_scope.hs_physics: A staple Bagrut mechanics question type — horizontal or angled launch with 3–4 sub-parts (range, max height, flight time, impact velocity). g = 10 m/s² is standard; answers must include units and clear decomposition.

Central to the mechanics questionnaire; free-body diagrams and ΣF = ma appear in nearly every exam. Typical multi-part problems cover Atwood machines, inclines, tension, and connected masses with explicit FBD sketches.

concepts.name: Friction
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Problems combining friction and Newton's laws

level_scope.hs_physics: Usually tested combined with Newton's laws on inclines or horizontal surfaces — not as an isolated topic. Expect μₛ vs μₖ distinction, friction direction, and whether motion starts or continues at constant speed.

concepts.name: Circular Motion
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Circular motion on flat road (friction provides centripetal force)

level_scope.hs_physics: Bagrut mechanics includes centripetal force problems — flat curves, banked roads, vertical loops, and conical pendulums. Questions identify the force providing F_c and link ω, v, r, and T.

concepts.name: Gravitation
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Newton's law of gravitation: F = Gm₁m₂/r²

level_scope.hs_physics: Appears in mechanics as satellite/orbit and escape-velocity problems using F = Gm₁m₂/r² and Kepler's third law. Less frequent than circular motion on a string, but a full multi-part gravitation question is common in mock exams.

Regular mechanics questionnaire material — work by a force at an angle, KE/PE, and the work-energy theorem. Typical items compare methods (energy vs Newton) on inclines, springs, or lifting problems with efficiency sub-parts.

Bagrut favorites include roller coasters, pendulums, and spring-block systems with and without friction. Expect E_initial = E_final (or accounting for W_friction) and qualitative energy bar/diagram interpretation.

concepts.name: Momentum & Impulse
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Newton's 2nd law in terms of momentum
Elastic collisions: both KE and p conserved

level_scope.hs_physics: Impulse and momentum conservation are tested in mechanics — often linked to collisions or explosions. Questions distinguish elastic vs inelastic outcomes and may require 2D vector momentum components.

Focused collision problems — head-on elastic/inelastic, coefficient of restitution, and ballistic-pendulum setups. Bagrut items usually give masses and initial speeds and ask for post-collision velocities or maximum swing height.

concepts.name: Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM)
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Position, velocity, acceleration as functions of time
Energy in SHM: KE + PE = constant

level_scope.hs_physics: Spring-mass and simple-pendulum period formulas (T = 2π√(m/k), T = 2π√(L/g)) appear in mechanics; SHM also bridges to AC circuits. Questions ask for period, amplitude, or energy exchange at turning points — no differential equations required.

concepts.name: Torque & Static Equilibrium
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Conditions for static equilibrium: ΣF=0 and Στ=0
Balancing a beam on a pivot
Uniform beam supported at two points

level_scope.hs_physics: Static equilibrium with torques — ladder-on-wall and beam-on-pivot problems are classic Bagrut mechanics items. Both ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0 must be applied; center of gravity location is often a sub-part.

concepts.name: Extended Static Equilibrium
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Stability and center of mass position

level_scope.hs_physics: Extended torque equilibrium beyond single-pivot cases — distributed loads, multi-support beams, and stability/tipping criteria. Less frequent than basic ladder problems but appears as a harder mechanics sub-question.

concepts.name: Rotational Kinematics
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Relationship between linear and angular: v=rω, a=rα

level_scope.hs_physics: Rotational analogues of linear kinematics (θ, ω, α) with v = rω links — tested when combined with rotational dynamics or rolling. Bagrut depth is formula-based conversion, not calculus of rotation.

Moment of inertia, τ = Iα, and angular-momentum conservation — including rolling-without-slipping on inclines. A full rotational-dynamics question is less guaranteed than linear mechanics but common in 5-unit mocks.

Core radiation-questionnaire (קרינה וחומר) material — v = fλ, standing waves on strings, and interference basics. Questions often combine SHM with wave speed and harmonic frequencies on a stretched string.

concepts.name: Sound Waves
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Nature of sound: longitudinal pressure wave
Speed of sound in different media

level_scope.hs_physics: Sound as a longitudinal wave — speed in media, intensity/decibels at conceptual level, beats, and resonance in pipes/strings. Typical radiation-chapter items ask for frequency relationships or explain standing-wave patterns in air columns.

Doppler frequency shift for moving source or observer — a standard radiation-topic calculation. Bagrut questions give speeds and rest frequency and ask for observed frequency or qualitative shift direction (approaching vs receding).

concepts.name: Geometric Optics
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Plane mirror: image location and properties
Concave and convex mirrors: focal length

level_scope.hs_physics: Major radiation-questionnaire topic — mirror/lens equations (1/f = 1/do + 1/di), Snell's law, total internal reflection, and ray diagrams. Multi-part items locate images, compute magnification, and classify real vs virtual.

Wave optics in the radiation chapter — Young's double-slit, path-difference interference conditions, and basic diffraction/polarization concepts. Calculations use Δx = mλ/2 or similar; no full electromagnetic-wave derivations.

concepts.name: Electrostatics
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Electric field of a point charge: E = kq/r²

level_scope.hs_physics: Opening topic of the electricity questionnaire (036-371) — Coulomb's law, field of point charges, and superposition. Typical items compute force or field magnitude/direction and sketch field lines for simple charge configurations.

concepts.name: Electric Field & Potential
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Work by electric field: W = qΔV
Motion of charged particle in electric field
Uniform electric field between plates: E = V/d

level_scope.hs_physics: Electric potential, ΔV, and motion of charges in uniform fields (E = V/d) — central to electricity exams. Questions link work W = qΔV to kinetic energy gained and trajectories between parallel plates.

Capacitor C = Q/V, parallel-plate formula, stored energy, and series/parallel combinations — tested within electricity multi-part problems. Expect equivalent capacitance and energy before/after reconfiguration.

DC circuit fundamentals — Ohm's law, series/parallel resistors, EMF with internal resistance, and P = IV. Almost every electricity exam includes a circuit calculation with ammeter/voltmeter placement and power/energy sub-parts.

concepts.name: Kirchhoff's Laws
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: KCL: sum of currents at node = 0
KVL: sum of voltages in loop = 0

level_scope.hs_physics: KCL and KVL for multi-loop and multi-node DC circuits — a hallmark electricity-questionnaire problem type. Students set up junction and loop equations; bridge/Wheatstone configurations appear as harder variants.

concepts.name: Magnetism & Magnetic Forces
concepts.subject: physics

Force on a current-carrying wire: F = BIL·sinθ
Force on moving charge: F = qv×B (Lorentz force)
Magnetic field inside solenoid: B = μ₀nI
Circular motion of charge in magnetic field

level_scope.hs_physics: Magnetic force on wires and moving charges (F = BIL, F = qvB), right-hand rule, and circular motion in B fields. Electricity items often combine Lorentz force with uniform E and B fields or solenoid field formulas.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic Induction
concepts.subject: physics
skill_atoms: EMF of a moving conductor in magnetic field: EMF = BLv
Energy stored in inductor: U = ½LI²

level_scope.hs_physics: Faraday's law, Lenz's law, motional EMF (BLv), and transformers — core electricity questionnaire content. Questions compute induced EMF/current direction, flux change, and ideal transformer voltage ratios.

concepts.name: AC Circuits
concepts.subject: physics

level_scope.hs_physics: AC circuits with X_C, X_L, impedance, and LC resonance — advanced electricity material for 5-unit Bagrut. Typical items use V_rms, phasor-style reasoning (sinusoidal sources), and find resonant frequency or power factor conceptually.

concepts.name: Atomic Models & Hydrogen Spectrum

level_scope.hs_physics: Bohr model and hydrogen spectrum — energy levels E_n = −13.6/n² eV and ΔE = hf for emission/absorption lines. Bagrut questions identify spectral series (especially Balmer) and compute photon wavelength or energy from level transitions.

concepts.name: Nuclear Physics & Radioactivity

level_scope.hs_physics: Radioactive decay equations, half-life N(t) = N₀(½)^(t/T½), activity, and E = mc² binding-energy problems — standard radiation-chapter material. Multi-part items balance nuclear equations and compute remaining activity or mass defect.

level_scope.hs_physics: Introductory special relativity at Bagrut depth — time dilation and length contraction formulas with v ≪ c checks; c as speed limit. Usually one calculation sub-part tied to modern-physics or nuclear context, not full Lorentz transformations.

level_scope.hs_physics: Static equilibrium with torques — ladder-on-wall and beam-on-pivot problems are classic Bagrut mechanics items. Both ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0 must be applied; center of gravity location is often a sub-part.

static_equilibrium.name: Extended Static Equilibrium
static_equilibrium.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Stability and center of mass position

level_scope.hs_physics: Extended torque equilibrium beyond single-pivot cases — distributed loads, multi-support beams, and stability/tipping criteria. Less frequent than basic ladder problems but appears as a harder mechanics sub-question.

rotational_kinematics.name: Rotational Kinematics
rotational_kinematics.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Relationship between linear and angular: v=rω, a=rα

level_scope.hs_physics: Rotational analogues of linear kinematics (θ, ω, α) with v = rω links — tested when combined with rotational dynamics or rolling. Bagrut depth is formula-based conversion, not calculus of rotation.

Moment of inertia, τ = Iα, and angular-momentum conservation — including rolling-without-slipping on inclines. A full rotational-dynamics question is less guaranteed than linear mechanics but common in 5-unit mocks.

Core radiation-questionnaire (קרינה וחומר) material — v = fλ, standing waves on strings, and interference basics. Questions often combine SHM with wave speed and harmonic frequencies on a stretched string.

sound_waves.name: Sound Waves
sound_waves.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Nature of sound: longitudinal pressure wave
Speed of sound in different media

level_scope.hs_physics: Sound as a longitudinal wave — speed in media, intensity/decibels at conceptual level, beats, and resonance in pipes/strings. Typical radiation-chapter items ask for frequency relationships or explain standing-wave patterns in air columns.

Doppler frequency shift for moving source or observer — a standard radiation-topic calculation. Bagrut questions give speeds and rest frequency and ask for observed frequency or qualitative shift direction (approaching vs receding).

optics_geometric.name: Geometric Optics
optics_geometric.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Plane mirror: image location and properties
Concave and convex mirrors: focal length

level_scope.hs_physics: Major radiation-questionnaire topic — mirror/lens equations (1/f = 1/do + 1/di), Snell's law, total internal reflection, and ray diagrams. Multi-part items locate images, compute magnification, and classify real vs virtual.

Wave optics in the radiation chapter — Young's double-slit, path-difference interference conditions, and basic diffraction/polarization concepts. Calculations use Δx = mλ/2 or similar; no full electromagnetic-wave derivations.

electrostatics.name: Electrostatics
electrostatics.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Electric field of a point charge: E = kq/r²

level_scope.hs_physics: Opening topic of the electricity questionnaire (036-371) — Coulomb's law, field of point charges, and superposition. Typical items compute force or field magnitude/direction and sketch field lines for simple charge configurations.

electric_field.name: Electric Field & Potential
electric_field.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Work by electric field: W = qΔV
Motion of charged particle in electric field
Uniform electric field between plates: E = V/d

level_scope.hs_physics: Electric potential, ΔV, and motion of charges in uniform fields (E = V/d) — central to electricity exams. Questions link work W = qΔV to kinetic energy gained and trajectories between parallel plates.

Capacitor C = Q/V, parallel-plate formula, stored energy, and series/parallel combinations — tested within electricity multi-part problems. Expect equivalent capacitance and energy before/after reconfiguration.

DC circuit fundamentals — Ohm's law, series/parallel resistors, EMF with internal resistance, and P = IV. Almost every electricity exam includes a circuit calculation with ammeter/voltmeter placement and power/energy sub-parts.

kirchhoff_laws.name: Kirchhoff's Laws
kirchhoff_laws.subject: physics
skill_atoms: KCL: sum of currents at node = 0
KVL: sum of voltages in loop = 0

level_scope.hs_physics: KCL and KVL for multi-loop and multi-node DC circuits — a hallmark electricity-questionnaire problem type. Students set up junction and loop equations; bridge/Wheatstone configurations appear as harder variants.

magnetism.name: Magnetism & Magnetic Forces
magnetism.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Magnetic field of a long wire: B = μ₀I/(2πr)
Force on a current-carrying wire: F = BIL·sinθ
Force on moving charge: F = qv×B (Lorentz force)
Magnetic field inside solenoid: B = μ₀nI
Circular motion of charge in magnetic field

level_scope.hs_physics: Magnetic force on wires and moving charges (F = BIL, F = qvB), right-hand rule, and circular motion in B fields. Electricity items often combine Lorentz force with uniform E and B fields or solenoid field formulas.

electromagnetic_induction.name: Electromagnetic Induction
electromagnetic_induction.subject: physics
skill_atoms: EMF of a moving conductor in magnetic field: EMF = BLv
Energy stored in inductor: U = ½LI²

level_scope.hs_physics: Faraday's law, Lenz's law, motional EMF (BLv), and transformers — core electricity questionnaire content. Questions compute induced EMF/current direction, flux change, and ideal transformer voltage ratios.

ac_circuits.name: AC Circuits
ac_circuits.subject: physics
skill_atoms: AC voltage and current: V = V₀·sin(ωt)

level_scope.hs_physics: AC circuits with X_C, X_L, impedance, and LC resonance — advanced electricity material for 5-unit Bagrut. Typical items use V_rms, phasor-style reasoning (sinusoidal sources), and find resonant frequency or power factor conceptually.

modern_physics_intro.name: Quantum Physics Basics (Photoelectric Effect)
modern_physics_intro.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Photoelectric effect: light ejects electrons from metal
Work function: minimum energy to eject electron
Einstein's photoelectric equation: KE_max = hf - φ

level_scope.hs_physics: Photoelectric effect and photon energy E = hf — anchor topic of the radiation questionnaire. Exam items use Einstein's equation KE_max = hf − φ, threshold frequency, and qualitative wave-particle duality; de Broglie may appear as a short calculation.

atomic_models.name: Atomic Models & Hydrogen Spectrum
atomic_models.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Photon emission and absorption: ΔE = hf

level_scope.hs_physics: Bohr model and hydrogen spectrum — energy levels E_n = −13.6/n² eV and ΔE = hf for emission/absorption lines. Bagrut questions identify spectral series (especially Balmer) and compute photon wavelength or energy from level transitions.

nuclear_physics.name: Nuclear Physics & Radioactivity
nuclear_physics.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Nucleus: protons, neutrons; atomic number Z, mass number A

level_scope.hs_physics: Radioactive decay equations, half-life N(t) = N₀(½)^(t/T½), activity, and E = mc² binding-energy problems — standard radiation-chapter material. Multi-part items balance nuclear equations and compute remaining activity or mass defect.

special_relativity.name: Special Relativity (Basic)
special_relativity.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Speed of light as universal speed limit
Mass-energy: E = mc² (primarily for nuclear problems)

level_scope.hs_physics: Introductory special relativity at Bagrut depth — time dilation and length contraction formulas with v ≪ c checks; c as speed limit. Usually one calculation sub-part tied to modern-physics or nuclear context, not full Lorentz transformations.

work_energy_conservation.name: Conservation of Mechanical Energy
work_energy_conservation.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Conservation: KE_i + PE_i = KE_f + PE_f (no friction)
Finding speed at a position from height

level_scope.hs_physics: Mechanics questionnaire — frictionless energy conservation; roller-coaster multi-part
Mechanics — collision problems; distinguish KE conservation vs momentum only

circular_motion_gravitation.name: Circular Motion & Gravitation
circular_motion_gravitation.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Vertical loop minimum speed at top

level_scope.hs_physics: Mechanics — combine circular motion with gravitation in orbit problems

coulomb_law.name: Coulomb's Law & Electric Force
coulomb_law.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Superposition of forces from multiple charges
Equilibrium of charges on a line

level_scope.hs_physics: Electricity questionnaire — force between point charges; vector addition

electric_field_potential.name: Electric Field & Potential
electric_field_potential.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Field of point charge E = kq/r²
Uniform field between plates E = V/d
Motion of charge in uniform E field

level_scope.hs_physics: Electricity — field lines, potential difference, and particle motion

dc_circuits_kirchhoff.name: DC Circuits — Kirchhoff's Laws
dc_circuits_kirchhoff.subject: physics
skill_atoms: KCL: sum of currents at a node = 0
KVL: sum of voltages around a loop = 0
Sign conventions for EMF and resistors

level_scope.hs_physics: Electricity questionnaire — multi-loop circuit analysis; guaranteed in mocks
Electricity — capacitor energy and combination problems

magnetic_force.name: Magnetic Force on Charges & Wires
magnetic_force.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Force on moving charge F = qvB sinθ
Force on current-carrying wire F = BIL sinθ
Circular motion of charge in uniform B field
Lorentz force with E and B combined

level_scope.hs_physics: Electricity — Lorentz force; circular path of charged particle in B

faraday_induction.name: Faraday's Law & Induction
faraday_induction.subject: physics
skill_atoms: EMF of moving rod EMF = BLv

level_scope.hs_physics: Electricity — flux change induces EMF; Lenz direction is exam favourite
Radiation questionnaire — Snell law calculations and TIR qualitative

em_waves.name: Electromagnetic Waves
em_waves.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Wave speed c = fλ in vacuum
Transverse E and B fields oscillating

level_scope.hs_physics: Radiation — spectrum ordering, c = fλ, link from induction to EM wave

photoelectric_effect.name: Photoelectric Effect
photoelectric_effect.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Intensity vs frequency effects on photoelectrons

level_scope.hs_physics: Radiation questionnaire — KE vs frequency linear graph; threshold frequency

newton_laws_general.name: Newton's Laws — General Applications
newton_laws_general.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Weight W = mg vs normal force
Tension in strings and Atwood machine
Inclined planes with and without friction

level_scope.hs_physics: Mechanics questionnaire core — FBD + ΣF=ma in nearly every exam
Mechanics — work at an angle, power, and efficiency sub-parts
Radiation — mirror/lens equation multi-part; ray diagram sketch

uni_vectors.name: Vector Calculus for Physics
uni_vectors.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Scalar vs vector quantities in physical contexts
Unit vectors and direction angles with quadrant correction
Dot product: magnitude, angle, and perpendicularity test
Cross product via determinant and right-hand rule
Choosing dot vs cross for physics (work, torque, magnetic force)
Resolving forces and velocities into x-y (and z) components
3D angle between vectors via dot product and arccos

level_scope.physics1: Full 2D/3D vector algebra with dot and cross products, unit-vector normalization, and physics applications (F = qv × B, W = F·d). Expect component-first problem solving at university exam depth.

uni_kinematics.name: Advanced Kinematics
uni_kinematics.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Displacement vs distance; velocity vs speed
Sign conventions and free-fall near Earth's surface
Selecting the appropriate kinematic equation for unknowns
Multi-stage motion (projectile from height, two-phase trajectories)
Interpreting x-t, v-t, and a-t graphs
Average vs instantaneous velocity under constant acceleration
Integrating v(t) and a(t) to recover position (calculus link)

level_scope.physics1: Constant-acceleration 1D kinematics at university rigor — multi-step problems, sign discipline, and equation selection. Calculus-based derivations of v(t) and x(t) are fair game; free-fall and relative-motion word problems are core.

uni_newtonian_mechanics.name: Newtonian Mechanics
uni_newtonian_mechanics.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Newton's three laws: inertia, F_net = ma, action-reaction pairs
Free body diagrams for single and connected objects
Weight, normal force, tension, and applied forces on FBDs
Component-wise Newton's 2nd law (ΣF_x = ma_x, ΣF_y = ma_y)
Elevator problems and apparent weight N = m(g ± a)
Connected blocks and string tension on frictionless surfaces
Atwood machine — derive and apply a and T formulas
Inclined plane with friction (N = mg cos θ, f = μN)
Multi-body systems — internal vs external forces
Combining Newton's 2nd law with kinematics for distance/speed

level_scope.physics1: Systematic FBD → ΣF = ma workflow for single bodies, connected masses, elevators, and Atwood machines. University exams expect derived formulas, limiting-case checks, and friction on inclines — not just plug-and-chug F = ma.

uni_work_energy.name: Work, Energy & Conservation Laws
uni_work_energy.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Work definition W = Fd cos θ and vector dot-product form
Conservation of mechanical energy (with and without friction)
Power P = Fv and rate of energy transfer
Non-conservative work and energy dissipation to heat
Choosing energy vs force methods for a given scenario

level_scope.physics1: Work, KE/PE, work-energy theorem, and mechanical-energy conservation at university depth — including friction losses and spring systems. Energy methods should be preferred when path-dependent forces are absent; dot-product work is assumed.

uni_momentum.name: Linear & Angular Momentum
uni_momentum.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Conservation of momentum in isolated systems
Elastic collisions in 1D (momentum and KE both conserved)
Impulse with sign reversal (wall bounce, F-t graph area)
KE loss fraction in inelastic collisions
Identifying collision type from problem wording

level_scope.physics1: Linear momentum, impulse, and 1D collisions at university depth — elastic vs inelastic classification, sign conventions, and explicit KE-loss analysis. Angular momentum appears in uni_rigid_body; here the focus is translational p and J.

uni_rigid_body.name: Rigid Body Dynamics
uni_rigid_body.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Torque τ = r × F and direction via right-hand rule
Moment of inertia I for standard shapes (disk, sphere, rod, hoop)
Newton's 2nd law for rotation τ_net = Iα
Parallel axis theorem I = I_cm + Md²
Rolling without slipping condition v = Rω
Total KE of rolling body (translational + rotational)
Combined F = ma and τ = Iα for rolling systems
Angular momentum L = Iω and conservation with no external torque
Tabulated I values and when to apply parallel-axis shift

level_scope.physics1: Rotational dynamics at Physics 1 depth — τ = Iα, standard I formulas, parallel-axis theorem, rolling energy splits, and ramp-race ranking via I/(MR²). Expect simultaneous translation + rotation analysis, not just memorized I tables.

uni_oscillations.name: Oscillations & Waves
uni_oscillations.subject: physics
skill_atoms: SHM total energy E = ½kA² conserved
KE/PE exchange and speed at position v = ω√(A² − x²)
Maximum speed v_max = Aω and ω = √(k/m)
Simple pendulum small-angle SHM equation of motion
Pendulum period T = 2π√(L/g) and mass independence
Derivation of pendulum EOM via tangential Newton's 2nd law
Where kinetic equals potential at x = ±A/√2
Energy-method protocol for SHM without tracking time
Distinguishing spring vs pendulum ω relationships

level_scope.physics1: SHM via energy conservation and small-angle pendulum theory — derive T = 2π√(L/g), compute speeds/energy fractions at arbitrary x, and justify the small-angle approximation. Wave propagation is deferred to later EM/optics concepts.

uni_fluids.name: Fluid Mechanics
uni_fluids.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Continuity equation A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ for incompressible flow
Bernoulli's equation and energy per unit volume
Fast flow → lower static pressure (Venturi / lift intuition)
Applying continuity first, then Bernoulli for pressures
Pipe narrowing and flow-speed calculation from radii
Venturi meter and real-world Bernoulli applications
Unit and sign checks in fluid-energy problems

level_scope.physics1: Ideal-fluid continuity + Bernoulli at intro-university depth — sequential continuity-then-Bernoulli workflow, Torricelli draining, and the counter-intuitive pressure–speed tradeoff. Viscosity and full hydrostatics are out of scope for this aliased lesson.

uni_thermodynamics.name: Thermodynamics
uni_thermodynamics.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Sensible heat Q = mcΔT within a single phase
Latent heat at phase change Q = mL (plateau regions)
First law of thermodynamics ΔU = Q − W (sign conventions)
Ideal gas law PV = nRT with Kelvin temperature
Isothermal, adiabatic, isochoric, and isobaric process simplifications
Multi-stage heating curves (heat, melt, heat, boil, …)
Internal energy change from heat in minus work out
Water-specific constants (c, L_f, L_v) and unit conversion (g ↔ kg)
Identifying process type from problem wording

level_scope.physics1: Makhina-aligned thermodynamics — calorimetry, latent heat, first law, and ideal-gas processes at rigorous SI-unit depth. Multi-stage heating-curve problems and explicit ΔU = Q − W sign discipline are expected; statistical mechanics is out of scope.

uni_electric_fields.name: Electric Fields & Gauss's Law
uni_electric_fields.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Coulomb's law and superposition for point charges
Electric field E = F/q as a vector field
Field of dipole and continuous charge distributions
Symmetry choice for Gaussian surfaces (sphere, cylinder, plane)
Field of infinite line/plane/shell from Gauss's law

level_scope.physics1: Electrostatics at university depth — Coulomb superposition, field lines, and Gauss's law with symmetry arguments on finals.

uni_potential.name: Electric Potential
uni_potential.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Potential of point charge V = kq/r
Equipotential surfaces perpendicular to field lines
Potential energy U = qV for charge in field
Relation E = −∇V (field as negative gradient of potential)

level_scope.physics1: Scalar potential methods for electrostatics; equipotentials and energy bookkeeping replace repeated vector superposition when possible.

uni_capacitance.name: Capacitance & Dielectrics
uni_capacitance.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Dielectric constant κ and field reduction in matter

level_scope.physics1: Capacitors at intro E&M depth — combination rules, stored energy, and dielectric modification of Gauss's-law problems.

uni_dc_circuits.name: DC Circuits
uni_dc_circuits.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Ohm's law V = IR and power P = IV
Multi-loop circuit analysis with sign conventions

level_scope.physics1: DC circuit analysis via Kirchhoff rules; multi-loop sign discipline and equivalent resistance are standard exam skills.

uni_magnetic_fields.name: Magnetic Fields & Forces
uni_magnetic_fields.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Lorentz force F = qv×B and right-hand rule
Force on current-carrying wire I L×B
Circular motion of charge in uniform B (r = mv/qB)
Biot–Savart / Ampère's law for symmetric geometries
Field of long straight wire and solenoid
Torque on magnetic dipole τ = μ×B

level_scope.physics1: Magnetism chapter — Lorentz force, wire forces, and symmetric B-field calculations using Ampère/Biot–Savart patterns.

uni_induction.name: Faraday's Law & Induction
uni_induction.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Induced electric field from changing flux

level_scope.physics1: Electromagnetic induction — flux change, Lenz sign rule, motional emf, and intro inductance on university E&M exams.

uni_ac_circuits.name: AC Circuits
uni_ac_circuits.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Sinusoidal AC voltage/current and angular frequency ω
Capacitive and inductive reactance X_C, X_L
Impedance Z in RLC series circuits

level_scope.physics1: Intro AC circuits with phasors and impedance; RLC resonance and power factor at university physics-2 bridge depth.

uni_maxwell.name: Maxwell's Equations
uni_maxwell.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Gauss's law for electricity and magnetism (no magnetic monopoles)
Faraday's law and Ampère–Maxwell law with displacement current
Consistency of wave solution from coupled E and B fields
Symmetry between changing E and B fields

level_scope.physics1: Maxwell's equations as capstone E&M — identify each law, displacement current role, and how EM waves emerge.

uni_em_waves.name: Electromagnetic Waves
uni_em_waves.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Transverse EM wave: E, B, and propagation direction mutually perpendicular
Energy density and Poynting vector S = E×B/μ₀
Spectrum from radio to gamma (frequency–wavelength relation)

level_scope.physics1: EM wave properties after Maxwell — polarization, intensity, spectrum, and Poynting-vector energy transport.

uni_optics.name: Wave Optics
uni_optics.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Thin-film interference and phase shifts on reflection
Diffraction grating d sin θ = mλ

level_scope.physics1: Wave optics — interference and diffraction quantitative conditions; connects SHM/wave language to light experiments.

uni_quantum_intro.name: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics
uni_quantum_intro.subject: physics
skill_atoms: Photoelectric effect and photon energy E = hf
Wave–particle duality for light and matter
Bohr model energy levels and spectral lines

level_scope.physics1: Intro quantum phenomena — photoelectric effect, de Broglie waves, and Bohr model at modern-physics survey depth.
